To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of cancer symptom guides by radiation therapists was influenced by a number of factors, including the perceived usefulness and ease of use of the guides, the support and encouragement of their supervisors and colleagues, the time required to use the guides, and the lack of time and resources for professional development.
The most common reasons for not using symptom guides were that they are too time-consuming, they do not provide the information required, and they are not relevant to the patient.

1) the most important factors influencing the use by therapists of the symptom guides were their perceived usefulness, ease of use, and perceived compatibility with their practice; and 2) therapists’ perceived usefulness of the guides was influenced by the perceived importance of symptoms to their practice, and the perceived ease of use by therapists was influenced by their perceptions of the guides’ user-friendliness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of symptom guides by radiation therapists in the treatment of people with cancer and the factors influencing their use.
the use of cancer symptom guidelines by radiation therapists.
the use by radiation therapy (RT) professionals of cancer symptom guides (CSGs).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation therapy community is ready to use symptom guides, but that the guides must be easy to use and have the support of their institutions to be successful.
there is no single factor that can be identified as the most influential factor in the use of symptom guides by radiation therapists.

the use of the symptom guides by radiation therapists was influenced by a variety of factors including the radiation therapists' knowledge of the symptom guides and the perceived usefulness of the symptom guides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation therapy providers should consider using symptom guides to support their patients.
the use of symptom guides is influenced by many factors, including the perceived benefits and barriers of using symptom guides, and the availability of resources.
